1→//! HKDF-SHA256 deterministic IPNS keypair derivation.
     2→//!
     3→//! Derives deterministic Ed25519 IPNS keypairs from a secp256k1 private key
     4→//! using HKDF-SHA256 with domain-separated info strings. Matches the TypeScript
     5→//! implementations in `@cipherbox/crypto` (vault/derive-ipns.ts, file/derive-ipns.ts,
     6→//! registry/derive-ipns.ts).
     7→//!
     8→//! Derivation path:
     9→//!   secp256k1 privateKey (32 bytes)
    10→//!     -> HKDF-SHA256(salt="CipherBox-v1", info=<domain-specific>)
    11→//!     -> 32-byte Ed25519 seed
    12→//!     -> Ed25519 keypair
    13→//!     -> IPNS name (k51...)
    14→
    15→use ed25519_dalek::SigningKey;
    16→use hkdf::Hkdf;
    17→use sha2::Sha256;
    18→use thiserror::Error;
    19→use zeroize::{Zeroize, Zeroizing};
    20→
    21→use super::ipns;
    22→
    23→/// Common HKDF salt for all CipherBox derivations.
    24→const HKDF_SALT: &[u8] = b"CipherBox-v1";
    25→
    26→/// HKDF info for vault IPNS keypair derivation (root folder metadata).
    27→const VAULT_HKDF_INFO: &[u8] = b"cipherbox-vault-ipns-v1";
    28→
    29→/// HKDF info for vault key blob IPNS keypair derivation (rootFolderKey storage).
    30→const VAULT_KEY_HKDF_INFO: &[u8] = b"cipherbox-vault-key-ipns-v1";
    31→
    32→/// HKDF info for device registry IPNS keypair derivation.
    33→const REGISTRY_HKDF_INFO: &[u8] = b"cipherbox-device-registry-ipns-v1";
    34→
    35→/// HKDF info for recycle bin IPNS keypair derivation.
    36→const BIN_HKDF_INFO: &[u8] = b"cipherbox-recycle-bin-ipns-v1";
    37→
    38→/// HKDF info prefix for per-file IPNS keypair derivation.
    39→const FILE_HKDF_INFO_PREFIX: &str = "cipherbox-file-ipns-v1:";
    40→
    41→/// Minimum file ID length (matches TypeScript validation).
    42→const MIN_FILE_ID_LENGTH: usize = 10;
    43→
    44→#[derive(Debug, Error)]
    45→pub enum HkdfError {
    46→    #[error("Invalid key size")]
    47→    InvalidKeySize,
    48→    #[error("HKDF derivation failed")]
    49→    DerivationFailed,
    50→    #[error("IPNS name derivation failed")]
    51→    IpnsDerivationFailed,
    52→    #[error("Invalid file ID: must be at least {MIN_FILE_ID_LENGTH} characters")]
    53→    InvalidFileId,
    54→}
    55→
    56→/// Internal helper: derive an Ed25519 keypair and IPNS name from HKDF output.
    57→///
    58→/// All three public functions follow the same pattern and delegate here.
    59→fn derive_ipns_keypair(
    60→    user_private_key: &[u8; 32],
    61→    info: &[u8],
    62→) -> Result<(Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>, Vec<u8>, String), HkdfError> {
    63→    // 1. HKDF-SHA256: extract + expand
    64→    let hk = Hkdf::<Sha256>::new(Some(HKDF_SALT), user_private_key);
    65→    let mut okm = [0u8; 32];
    66→    hk.expand(info, &mut okm)
    67→        .map_err(|_| HkdfError::DerivationFailed)?;
    68→
    69→    // 2. Ed25519 keypair from 32-byte seed
    70→    let signing_key = SigningKey::from_bytes(&okm);
    71→    okm.zeroize();
    72→    let verifying_key = signing_key.verifying_key();
    73→
    74→    let private_key = Zeroizing::new(signing_key.to_bytes().to_vec());
    75→    let public_key = verifying_key.to_bytes().to_vec();
    76→
    77→    // 3. Derive IPNS name from public key
    78→    let pk_array: [u8; 32] = verifying_key.to_bytes();
    79→    let ipns_name = ipns::derive_ipns_name(&pk_array).map_err(|_| HkdfError::IpnsDerivationFailed)?;
    80→
    81→    Ok((private_key, public_key, ipns_name))
    82→}
    83→
    84→/// Derive the deterministic Ed25519 IPNS keypair for the user's vault.
    85→///
    86→/// Uses HKDF info "cipherbox-vault-ipns-v1" for domain separation.
    87→///
    88→/// Given the same secp256k1 privateKey, this always produces the same
    89→/// IPNS name, enabling vault discovery from any device with the user's key.
    90→///
    91→/// Returns (ed25519_private_key, ed25519_public_key, ipns_name).
    92→pub fn derive_vault_ipns_keypair(
    93→    user_private_key: &[u8; 32],
    94→) -> Result<(Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>, Vec<u8>, String), HkdfError> {
    95→    derive_ipns_keypair(user_private_key, VAULT_HKDF_INFO)
    96→}
    97→
    98→/// Derive a dedicated Ed25519 IPNS keypair for the vault key blob.
    99→///
   100→/// This IPNS name stores the v2 blob containing the ECIES-wrapped rootFolderKey.
   101→/// Separate from the root folder IPNS name to avoid folder publishes overwriting the key blob.
   102→///
   103→/// Uses HKDF info "cipherbox-vault-key-ipns-v1" for domain separation.
   104→pub fn derive_vault_key_ipns_keypair(
   105→    user_private_key: &[u8; 32],
   106→) -> Result<(Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>, Vec<u8>, String), HkdfError> {
   107→    derive_ipns_keypair(user_private_key, VAULT_KEY_HKDF_INFO)
   108→}
   109→
   110→/// Derive a deterministic Ed25519 IPNS keypair for a specific file.
   111→///
   112→/// Uses HKDF info "cipherbox-file-ipns-v1:{fileId}" for per-file domain separation.
   113→///
   114→/// Returns (ed25519_private_key, ed25519_public_key, ipns_name).
   115→pub fn derive_file_ipns_keypair(
   116→    user_private_key: &[u8; 32],
   117→    file_id: &str,
   118→) -> Result<(Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>, Vec<u8>, String), HkdfError> {
   119→    if file_id.len() < MIN_FILE_ID_LENGTH {
   120→        return Err(HkdfError::InvalidFileId);
   121→    }
   122→
   123→    let info = format!("{}{}", FILE_HKDF_INFO_PREFIX, file_id);
   124→    derive_ipns_keypair(user_private_key, info.as_bytes())
   125→}
   126→
   127→/// Derive the deterministic Ed25519 IPNS keypair for the device registry.
   128→///
   129→/// Uses HKDF info "cipherbox-device-registry-ipns-v1" for domain separation.
   130→///
   131→/// Returns (ed25519_private_key, ed25519_public_key, ipns_name).
   132→pub fn derive_registry_ipns_keypair(
   133→    user_private_key: &[u8; 32],
   134→) -> Result<(Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>, Vec<u8>, String), HkdfError> {
   135→    derive_ipns_keypair(user_private_key, REGISTRY_HKDF_INFO)
   136→}
   137→
   138→/// Derive the deterministic Ed25519 IPNS keypair for the recycle bin.
   139→///
   140→/// Uses HKDF info "cipherbox-recycle-bin-ipns-v1" for domain separation.
   141→///
   142→/// Returns (ed25519_private_key, ed25519_public_key, ipns_name).
   143→pub fn derive_bin_ipns_keypair(
   144→    user_private_key: &[u8; 32],
   145→) -> Result<(Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>, Vec<u8>, String), HkdfError> {
   146→    derive_ipns_keypair(user_private_key, BIN_HKDF_INFO)
   147→}

1→//! Utility functions for cryptographic operations.
     2→
     3→use rand::RngCore;
     4→use thiserror::Error;
     5→use zeroize::Zeroize;
     6→
     7→use super::aes::{AES_IV_SIZE, AES_KEY_SIZE};
     8→
     9→#[derive(Debug, Error)]
    10→pub enum UtilError {
    11→    #[error("Invalid hex string")]
    12→    InvalidHex,
    13→}
    14→
    15→/// Generate cryptographically secure random bytes.
    16→pub fn generate_random_bytes(len: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
    17→    let mut buf = vec![0u8; len];
    18→    rand::rngs::OsRng.fill_bytes(&mut buf);
    19→    buf
    20→}
    21→
    22→/// Generate a random 32-byte AES key.
    23→pub fn generate_file_key() -> [u8; AES_KEY_SIZE] {
    24→    let mut key = [0u8; AES_KEY_SIZE];
    25→    rand::rngs::OsRng.fill_bytes(&mut key);
    26→    key
    27→}
    28→
    29→/// Generate a random 12-byte IV.
    30→pub fn generate_iv() -> [u8; AES_IV_SIZE] {
    31→    let mut iv = [0u8; AES_IV_SIZE];
    32→    rand::rngs::OsRng.fill_bytes(&mut iv);
    33→    iv
    34→}
    35→
    36→/// Convert a hex string to bytes.
    37→pub fn hex_to_bytes(hex: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>, UtilError> {
    38→    hex::decode(hex).map_err(|_| UtilError::InvalidHex)
    39→}
    40→
    41→/// Convert bytes to a hex string.
    42→pub fn bytes_to_hex(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
    43→    hex::encode(bytes)
    44→}
    45→
    46→/// Zeroize sensitive data in a byte slice.
    47→pub fn clear_bytes(buf: &mut [u8]) {
    48→    buf.zeroize();
    49→}
    50→
    51→/// Generate a random UUID v4 string.
    52→pub fn generate_uuid_v4() -> String {
    53→    let bytes = generate_random_bytes(16);
    54→    format!(
    55→        "{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}-{:02x}{:02x}-4{:01x}{:02x}-{:02x}{:02x}-{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}",
    56→        bytes[0], bytes[1], bytes[2], bytes[3],
    57→        bytes[4], bytes[5],
    58→        bytes[6] & 0x0f, bytes[7],
    59→        (bytes[8] & 0x3f) | 0x80, bytes[9],
    60→        bytes[10], bytes[11], bytes[12], bytes[13], bytes[14], bytes[15],
    61→    )
    62→}
    63→
    64→/// Detect MIME type from file extension.
    65→///
    66→/// Returns a static string to avoid heap allocation on hot paths.
    67→pub fn mime_from_extension(filename: &str) -> &'static str {
    68→    let ext = filename.rsplit('.').next().unwrap_or("");
    69→    // Use eq_ignore_ascii_case to avoid heap-allocating a lowercase copy
    70→    MIME_EXTENSIONS
    71→        .iter()
    72→        .find(|(e, _)| e.eq_ignore_ascii_case(ext))
    73→        .map(|(_, mime)| *mime)
    74→        .unwrap_or("application/octet-stream")
    75→}

1→//! Folder metadata types and encryption.
     2→//!
     3→//! Matches the TypeScript `FolderMetadata` type exactly.
     4→//! Uses Serde `rename_all = "camelCase"` to produce JSON field names
     5→//! identical to the TypeScript format.
     6→//!
     7→//! Only v2 schema (per-file IPNS pointers via FilePointer) is supported.
     8→//! v1 (inline file data) has been removed.
     9→
    10→use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
    11→use thiserror::Error;
    12→use zeroize::Zeroize;
    13→
    14→use super::aes::{self, AesError};
    15→
    16→#[derive(Debug, Error)]
    17→pub enum FolderError {
    18→    #[error("Encryption failed")]
    19→    EncryptionFailed(#[from] AesError),
    20→    #[error("Serialization failed")]
    21→    SerializationFailed,
    22→    #[error("Deserialization failed")]
    23→    DeserializationFailed,
    24→}
    25→
    26→/// Subfolder entry within folder metadata.
    27→/// Contains ECIES-wrapped keys for accessing the subfolder.
    28→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    29→#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
    30→pub struct FolderEntry {
    31→    /// UUID for internal reference.
    32→    pub id: String,
    33→    /// Folder name (plaintext, since whole metadata is encrypted).
    34→    pub name: String,
    35→    /// IPNS name for this subfolder (k51... format).
    36→    pub ipns_name: String,
    37→    /// Hex-encoded ECIES-wrapped AES-256 key for decrypting subfolder metadata.
    38→    pub folder_key_encrypted: String,
    39→    /// Hex-encoded ECIES-wrapped Ed25519 private key for IPNS signing.
    40→    pub ipns_private_key_encrypted: String,
    41→    /// Creation timestamp (Unix ms).
    42→    pub created_at: u64,
    43→    /// Last modification timestamp (Unix ms).
    44→    pub modified_at: u64,
    45→}
    46→
    47→/// Slim file reference stored in folder metadata.
    48→/// Points to a file's own IPNS record instead of embedding all file data inline.
    49→/// Matches TypeScript `FilePointer` from `@cipherbox/crypto/file/types.ts`.
    50→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    51→#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
    52→pub struct FilePointer {
    53→    /// UUID for internal reference.
    54→    pub id: String,
    55→    /// File name (plaintext, since folder metadata is encrypted).
    56→    pub name: String,
    57→    /// IPNS name of the file's own metadata record.
    58→    pub file_meta_ipns_name: String,
    59→    /// Hex-encoded ECIES-wrapped Ed25519 private key for signing this file's IPNS record.
    60→    /// Present for files created after the random-key migration. Absent for legacy files
    61→    /// whose IPNS key is derived deterministically via HKDF.
    62→    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    63→    #[serde(default)]
    64→    pub ipns_private_key_encrypted: Option<String>,
    65→    /// Creation timestamp (Unix ms).
    66→    pub created_at: u64,
    67→    /// Last modification timestamp (Unix ms).
    68→    pub modified_at: u64,
    69→}
    70→
    71→/// A child entry can be either a folder or a file pointer.
    72→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    73→#[serde(tag = "type", rename_all = "lowercase")]
    74→pub enum FolderChild {
    75→    /// A subfolder entry.
    76→    Folder(FolderEntry),
    77→    /// A file pointer referencing a per-file IPNS record.
    78→    File(FilePointer),
    79→}
    80→
    81→/// Decrypted folder metadata structure (v2 schema with per-file IPNS pointers).
    82→/// The entire FolderMetadata object is encrypted as a single blob with AES-256-GCM.
    83→/// Children can be FolderEntry (subfolder) or FilePointer (slim IPNS reference).
    84→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    85→pub struct FolderMetadata {
    86→    /// Schema version (always "v2").
    87→    pub version: String,
    88→    /// Folders and file pointers in this folder.
    89→    pub children: Vec<FolderChild>,
    90→}
    91→
    92→/// Encrypt folder metadata with AES-256-GCM.
    93→///
    94→/// JSON serializes the metadata, then seals with AES-GCM.
    95→/// Returns the sealed bytes: IV (12) || ciphertext || tag (16).
    96→pub fn encrypt_folder_metadata(
    97→    metadata: &FolderMetadata,
    98→    folder_key: &[u8; 32],
    99→) -> Result<Vec<u8>, FolderError> {
   100→    let mut json = serde_json::to_vec(metadata).map_err(|_| FolderError::SerializationFailed)?;
   101→    let result = aes::seal_aes_gcm(&json, folder_key).map_err(FolderError::EncryptionFailed);

   106→/// Decrypt folder metadata from AES-256-GCM sealed bytes.
   107→///
   108→/// Unseals, then JSON deserializes to FolderMetadata.
   109→/// Rejects metadata with version other than "v2".
   110→pub fn decrypt_folder_metadata(
   111→    sealed: &[u8],
   112→    folder_key: &[u8; 32],
   113→) -> Result<FolderMetadata, FolderError> {
   114→    let mut json = aes::unseal_aes_gcm(sealed, folder_key).map_err(FolderError::EncryptionFailed)?;
   115→
   116→    // Parse as generic JSON to check version field
   117→    let value: serde_json::Value =
   118→        serde_json::from_slice(&json).map_err(|e| {
   119→            log::error!("JSON parse failed: {}", e);
   120→            json.zeroize();
   121→            FolderError::DeserializationFailed
   122→        })?;
   123→
   124→    let version = value.get("version").and_then(|v| v.as_str());
   125→    if version != Some("v2") {
   126→        log::error!(
   127→            "Unsupported folder metadata version: {:?} (only v2 is supported)",
   128→            version
   129→        );
   130→        json.zeroize();
   131→        return Err(FolderError::DeserializationFailed);
   132→    }
   133→
   134→    let result: Result<FolderMetadata, _> = serde_json::from_value(value).map_err(|e| {
   135→        log::error!("V2 metadata deserialization failed: {}", e);
   136→        FolderError::DeserializationFailed
   137→    });
   138→
   139→    json.zeroize();
   140→    result
   141→}

   294→```rust
   295→//! Cross-language parity tests for cipherbox-crypto.
   296→//!
   297→//! Loads shared test vectors from tests/vectors/crypto/*.json
   298→//! and verifies Rust produces identical output to TypeScript.
   299→
   300→use serde::Deserialize;
   301→use std::path::PathBuf;
   302→
   303→fn vectors_path(subpath: &str) -> PathBuf {
   304→    let mut p = PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"));
   305→    p.push("../../tests/vectors");
   306→    p.push(subpath);
   307→    p
   308→}
   309→
   310→fn load_vectors<T: serde::de::DeserializeOwned>(filename: &str) -> Vec<T> {
   311→    let path = vectors_path(filename);
   312→    let data = std::fs::read_to_string(&path)
   313→        .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("Failed to load {}: {}", path.display(), e));
   314→    serde_json::from_str(&data).unwrap()
   315→}
   316→
   317→#[derive(Deserialize)]
   318→struct AesGcmVector {
   319→    key: String,
   320→    iv: String,
   321→    plaintext: String,
   322→    ciphertext: String,
   323→}
   324→
   325→#[test]
   326→fn aes_gcm_cross_language() {
   327→    let vectors: Vec<AesGcmVector> = load_vectors("crypto/aes-gcm.json");
   328→    assert!(!vectors.is_empty(), "No AES-GCM vectors loaded");
   329→    for v in &vectors {
   330→        let key = hex::decode(&v.key).unwrap();
   331→        let iv = hex::decode(&v.iv).unwrap();
   332→        let plaintext = hex::decode(&v.plaintext).unwrap();
   333→        let expected = hex::decode(&v.ciphertext).unwrap();
   334→
   335→        let key_arr: [u8; 32] = key.try_into().unwrap();
   336→        let iv_arr: [u8; 12] = iv.try_into().unwrap();
   337→
   338→        // Encrypt and verify
   339→        let encrypted = cipherbox_crypto::encrypt_aes_gcm(&plaintext, &key_arr, &iv_arr).unwrap();
   340→        assert_eq!(hex::encode(&encrypted), v.ciphertext, "AES-GCM encrypt mismatch");
   341→
   342→        // Decrypt and verify
   343→        let decrypted = cipherbox_crypto::decrypt_aes_gcm(&expected, &key_arr, &iv_arr).unwrap();
   344→        assert_eq!(hex::encode(&decrypted), v.plaintext, "AES-GCM decrypt mismatch");
   345→    }
   346→}
   347→
   348→// Similar test functions for:
   349→// - ed25519_cross_language (sign, verify, get_public_key)
   350→// - hkdf_cross_language (derive_vault_ipns_keypair, derive_vault_key_ipns_keypair, etc.)
   351→// - ipns_name_cross_language (derive_ipns_name)
   352→// - ecies_cross_language (wrap_key round-trip -- note: ECIES output is non-deterministic,
   353→//   so test round-trip not exact output match)
   354→```

1→<overview>
     2→Plans execute autonomously. Checkpoints formalize interaction points where human verification or decisions are needed.
     3→
     4→**Core principle:** Claude automates everything with CLI/API. Checkpoints are for verification and decisions, not manual work.
     5→
     6→**Golden rules:**
     7→
     8→1. **If Claude can run it, Claude runs it** - Never ask user to execute CLI commands, start servers, or run builds
     9→2. **Claude sets up the verification environment** - Start dev servers, seed databases, configure env vars
    10→3. **User only does what requires human judgment** - Visual checks, UX evaluation, "does this feel right?"
    11→4. **Secrets come from user, automation comes from Claude** - Ask for API keys, then Claude uses them via CLI
    12→5. **Auto-mode bypasses verification/decision checkpoints** — When `workflow._auto_chain_active` or `workflow.auto_advance` is true in config: human-verify auto-approves, decision auto-selects first option, human-action still stops (auth gates cannot be automated)
    13→   </overview>

   380→<authentication_gates>
   381→
   382→**Auth gate = Claude tried CLI/API, got auth error.** Not a failure — a gate requiring human input to unblock.
   383→
   384→**Pattern:** Claude tries automation → auth error → creates checkpoint:human-action → user authenticates → Claude retries → continues
   385→
   386→**Gate protocol:**
   387→
   388→1. Recognize it's not a failure - missing auth is expected
   389→2. Stop current task - don't retry repeatedly
   390→3. Create checkpoint:human-action dynamically
   391→4. Provide exact authentication steps
   392→5. Verify authentication works
   393→6. Retry the original task
   394→7. Continue normally
   395→
   396→**Key distinction:**
   397→
   398→- Pre-planned checkpoint: "I need you to do X" (wrong - Claude should automate)
   399→- Auth gate: "I tried to automate X but need credentials" (correct - unblocks automation)
   400→

   412→| Railway     | `railway`      | `init`, `up`, `variables set`             | `railway login`      |
   413→| Fly         | `fly`          | `launch`, `deploy`, `secrets set`         | `fly auth login`     |
   414→| Stripe      | `stripe` + API | `listen`, `trigger`, API calls            | API key in .env      |
   415→| Supabase    | `supabase`     | `init`, `link`, `db push`, `gen types`    | `supabase login`     |
   416→| Upstash     | `upstash`      | `redis create`, `redis get`               | `upstash auth login` |
   417→| PlanetScale | `pscale`       | `database create`, `branch create`        | `pscale auth login`  |
   418→| GitHub      | `gh`           | `repo create`, `pr create`, `secret set`  | `gh auth login`      |
   419→| Node        | `npm`/`pnpm`   | `install`, `run build`, `test`, `run dev` | N/A                  |
   420→| Xcode       | `xcodebuild`   | `-project`, `-scheme`, `build`, `test`    | N/A                  |
   421→| Convex      | `npx convex`   | `dev`, `deploy`, `env set`, `env get`     | `npx convex login`   |
   422→
   423→## Environment Variable Automation
   424→
   425→**Env files:** Use Write/Edit tools. Never ask human to create .env manually.
   426→
   427→**Dashboard env vars via CLI:**
   428→
   429→| Platform | CLI Command             | Example                                    |
   430→| -------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
   431→| Convex   | `npx convex env set`    | `npx convex env set OPENAI_API_KEY sk-...` |
   432→| Vercel   | `vercel env add`        | `vercel env add STRIPE_KEY production`     |
   433→| Railway  | `railway variables set` | `railway variables set API_KEY=value`      |
   434→| Fly      | `fly secrets set`       | `fly secrets set DATABASE_URL=...`         |
   435→| Supabase | `supabase secrets set`  | `supabase secrets set MY_SECRET=value`     |
   436→
   437→**Secret collection pattern:**
   438→
   439→```xml
   440→<!-- WRONG: Asking user to add env vars in dashboard -->
   441→<task type="checkpoint:human-action">
   442→  <action>Add OPENAI_API_KEY to Convex dashboard</action>
   443→  <instructions>Go to dashboard.convex.dev → Settings → Environment Variables → Add</instructions>
   444→</task>
   445→
   446→<!-- RIGHT: Claude asks for value, then adds via CLI -->
   447→<task type="checkpoint:human-action">
   448→  <action>Provide your OpenAI API key</action>
   449→  <instructions>
   450→    I need your OpenAI API key for Convex backend.
   451→    Get it from: https://platform.openai.com/api-keys
   452→    Paste the key (starts with sk-)
   453→  </instructions>
   454→  <verification>I'll add it via `npx convex env set` and verify</verification>
   455→  <resume-signal>Paste your API key</resume-signal>
   456→</task>
   457→
   458→<task type="auto">
   459→  <name>Configure OpenAI key in Convex</name>
   460→  <action>Run `npx convex env set OPENAI_API_KEY {user-provided-key}`</action>
   461→  <verify>`npx convex env get OPENAI_API_KEY` returns the key (masked)</verify>
   462→</task>
   463→```
   464→
   465→## Dev Server Automation
   466→
   467→| Framework | Start Command                | Ready Signal                   | Default URL           |
   468→| --------- | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------ | --------------------- |
   469→| Next.js   | `npm run dev`                | "Ready in" or "started server" | http://localhost:3000 |
   470→| Vite      | `npm run dev`                | "ready in"                     | http://localhost:5173 |
   471→| Convex    | `npx convex dev`             | "Convex functions ready"       | N/A (backend only)    |
   472→| Express   | `npm start`                  | "listening on port"            | http://localhost:3000 |
   473→| Django    | `python manage.py runserver` | "Starting development server"  | http://localhost:8000 |
   474→
   475→**Server lifecycle:**
   476→
   477→```bash
   478→# Run in background, capture PID
   479→npm run dev &
   480→DEV_SERVER_PID=$!
   481→
   482→# Wait for ready (max 30s) — uses fetch() for cross-platform compatibility
   483→timeout 30 bash -c 'until node -e "fetch(\"http://localhost:3000\").then(r=>{process.exit(r.ok?0:1)}).catch(()=>process.exit(1))" 2>/dev/null; do sleep 1; done'
   484→```
   485→
   486→**Port conflicts:** Kill stale process (`lsof -ti:3000 | xargs kill`) or use alternate port (`--port 3001`).
   487→
   488→**Server stays running** through checkpoints. Only kill when plan complete, switching to production, or port needed for different service.
   489→
   490→## CLI Installation Handling
   491→
   492→| CLI           | Auto-install? | Command                                               |
   493→| ------------- | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
   494→| npm/pnpm/yarn | No - ask user | User chooses package manager                          |
   495→| vercel        | Yes           | `npm i -g vercel`                                     |
   496→| gh (GitHub)   | Yes           | `brew install gh` (macOS) or `apt install gh` (Linux) |
   497→| stripe        | Yes           | `npm i -g stripe`                                     |
   498→| supabase      | Yes           | `npm i -g supabase`                                   |
   499→| convex        | No - use npx  | `npx convex` (no install needed)                      |
   500→| fly           | Yes           | `brew install flyctl` or curl installer               |
   501→| railway       | Yes           | `npm i -g @railway/cli`                               |
   502→
   503→**Protocol:** Try command → "command not found" → auto-installable? → yes: install silently, retry → no: checkpoint asking user to install.
   504→
   505→## Pre-Checkpoint Automation Failures
   506→
   507→| Failure            | Response                                                    |
   508→| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
   509→| Server won't start | Check error, fix issue, retry (don't proceed to checkpoint) |
   510→| Port in use        | Kill stale process or use alternate port                    |
   511→| Missing dependency | Run `npm install`, retry                                    |
   512→| Build error        | Fix the error first (bug, not checkpoint issue)             |
   513→| Auth error         | Create auth gate checkpoint                                 |
   514→| Network timeout    | Retry with backoff, then checkpoint if persistent           |
   515→
   516→**Never present a checkpoint with broken verification environment.** If the local server isn't responding, don't ask user to "visit localhost:3000".
   517→
   518→> **Cross-platform note:** Use `node -e "fetch('http://localhost:3000').then(r=>console.log(r.status))"` instead of `curl` for health checks. `curl` is broken on Windows MSYS/Git Bash due to SSL/path mangling issues.
   519→
   520→```xml
   521→<!-- WRONG: Checkpoint with broken environment -->
   522→<task type="checkpoint:human-verify">
   523→  <what-built>Dashboard (server failed to start)</what-built>
   524→  <how-to-verify>Visit http://localhost:3000...</how-to-verify>
   525→</task>
   526→
   527→<!-- RIGHT: Fix first, then checkpoint -->
   528→<task type="auto">
   529→  <name>Fix server startup issue</name>
   530→  <action>Investigate error, fix root cause, restart server</action>
   531→  <verify>fetch http://localhost:3000 returns 200</verify>
   532→</task>
   533→
   534→<task type="checkpoint:human-verify">
   535→  <what-built>Dashboard - server running at http://localhost:3000</what-built>
   536→  <how-to-verify>Visit http://localhost:3000/dashboard...</how-to-verify>
   537→</task>
   538→```
   539→
   540→## Automatable Quick Reference
   541→
   542→| Action                           | Automatable?               | Claude does it? |
   543→| -------------------------------- | -------------------------- | --------------- |
   544→| Deploy to Vercel                 | Yes (`vercel`)             | YES             |
   545→| Create Stripe webhook            | Yes (API)                  | YES             |
   546→| Write .env file                  | Yes (Write tool)           | YES             |
   547→| Create Upstash DB                | Yes (`upstash`)            | YES             |
   548→| Run tests                        | Yes (`npm test`)           | YES             |
   549→| Start dev server                 | Yes (`npm run dev`)        | YES             |
   550→| Add env vars to Convex           | Yes (`npx convex env set`) | YES             |
   551→| Add env vars to Vercel           | Yes (`vercel env add`)     | YES             |
   552→| Seed database                    | Yes (CLI/API)              | YES             |
   553→| Click email verification link    | No                         | NO              |
   554→| Enter credit card with 3DS       | No                         | NO              |
   555→| Complete OAuth in browser        | No                         | NO              |
   556→| Visually verify UI looks correct | No                         | NO              |
   557→| Test interactive user flows      | No                         | NO              |
   558→
   559→</automation_reference>
   560→
   561→<writing_guidelines>
   562→
   563→**DO:**
   564→
   565→- Automate everything with CLI/API before checkpoint
   566→- Be specific: "Visit https://myapp.vercel.app" not "check deployment"
   567→- Number verification steps
   568→- State expected outcomes: "You should see X"
   569→- Provide context: why this checkpoint exists
   570→
   571→**DON'T:**
   572→
   573→- Ask human to do work Claude can automate ❌
   574→- Assume knowledge: "Configure the usual settings" ❌
   575→- Skip steps: "Set up database" (too vague) ❌
   576→- Mix multiple verifications in one checkpoint ❌
   577→
   578→**Placement:**
   579→
   580→- **After automation completes** - not before Claude does the work
   581→- **After UI buildout** - before declaring phase complete
   582→- **Before dependent work** - decisions before implementation
   583→- **At integration points** - after configuring external services
   584→
   585→**Bad placement:** Before automation ❌ | Too frequent ❌ | Too late (dependent tasks already needed the result) ❌
   586→</writing_guidelines>
   587→
   588→<examples>
   589→
   590→### Example 1: Database Setup (No Checkpoint Needed)
   591→
   592→```xml
   593→<task type="auto">
   594→  <name>Create Upstash Redis database</name>
   595→  <files>.env</files>
   596→  <action>
   597→    1. Run `upstash redis create myapp-cache --region us-east-1`
   598→    2. Capture connection URL from output
   599→    3. Write to .env: UPSTASH_REDIS_URL={url}
   600→    4. Verify connection with test command
   601→  </action>
   602→  <verify>
   603→    - upstash redis list shows database
   604→    - .env contains UPSTASH_REDIS_URL
   605→    - Test connection succeeds
   606→  </verify>
   607→  <done>Redis database created and configured</done>
   608→</task>
   609→
   610→<!-- NO CHECKPOINT NEEDED - Claude automated everything and verified programmatically -->
   611→```
   612→
   613→### Example 2: Full Auth Flow (Single checkpoint at end)
   614→
   615→```xml
   616→<task type="auto">
   617→  <name>Create user schema</name>
   618→  <files>src/db/schema.ts</files>
   619→  <action>Define User, Session, Account tables with Drizzle ORM</action>
   620→  <verify>npm run db:generate succeeds</verify>
   621→</task>
   622→
   623→<task type="auto">
   624→  <name>Create auth API routes</name>
   625→  <files>src/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts</files>
   626→  <action>Set up NextAuth with GitHub provider, JWT strategy</action>
   627→  <verify>TypeScript compiles, no errors</verify>
   628→</task>
   629→
   630→<task type="auto">
   631→  <name>Create login UI</name>
   632→  <files>src/app/login/page.tsx, src/components/LoginButton.tsx</files>
   633→  <action>Create login page with GitHub OAuth button</action>
   634→  <verify>npm run build succeeds</verify>
   635→</task>
   636→
   637→<task type="auto">
   638→  <name>Start dev server for auth testing</name>
   639→  <action>Run `npm run dev` in background, wait for ready signal</action>
   640→  <verify>fetch http://localhost:3000 returns 200</verify>
   641→  <done>Dev server running at http://localhost:3000</done>
   642→</task>
   643→
   644→<!-- ONE checkpoint at end verifies the complete flow -->
   645→<task type="checkpoint:human-verify" gate="blocking">
   646→  <what-built>Complete authentication flow - dev server running at http://localhost:3000</what-built>
   647→  <how-to-verify>
   648→    1. Visit: http://localhost:3000/login
   649→    2. Click "Sign in with GitHub"
   650→    3. Complete GitHub OAuth flow
   651→    4. Verify: Redirected to /dashboard, user name displayed
   652→    5. Refresh page: Session persists
   653→    6. Click logout: Session cleared
   654→  </how-to-verify>
   655→  <resume-signal>Type "approved" or describe issues</resume-signal>
   656→</task>
   657→```
   658→
   659→</examples>
   660→
   661→<anti_patterns>
   662→
   663→### ❌ BAD: Asking user to start dev server
   664→
   665→```xml
   666→<task type="checkpoint:human-verify" gate="blocking">
   667→  <what-built>Dashboard component</what-built>
   668→  <how-to-verify>
   669→    1. Run: npm run dev
   670→    2. Visit: http://localhost:3000/dashboard
   671→    3. Check layout is correct
   672→  </how-to-verify>
   673→</task>
   674→```
   675→
   676→**Why bad:** Claude can run `npm run dev`. User should only visit URLs, not execute commands.
   677→
   678→### ✅ GOOD: Claude starts server, user visits
   679→
   680→```xml
   681→<task type="auto">
   682→  <name>Start dev server</name>
   683→  <action>Run `npm run dev` in background</action>
   684→  <verify>fetch http://localhost:3000 returns 200</verify>
   685→</task>
   686→
   687→<task type="checkpoint:human-verify" gate="blocking">
   688→  <what-built>Dashboard at http://localhost:3000/dashboard (server running)</what-built>
   689→  <how-to-verify>
   690→    Visit http://localhost:3000/dashboard and verify:
   691→    1. Layout matches design
   692→    2. No console errors
   693→  </how-to-verify>
   694→</task>
   695→```
   696→
   697→### ❌ BAD: Asking human to deploy / ✅ GOOD: Claude automates
   698→
   699→```xml
   700→<!-- BAD: Asking user to deploy via dashboard -->
   701→<task type="checkpoint:human-action" gate="blocking">
   702→  <action>Deploy to Vercel</action>
   703→  <instructions>Visit vercel.com/new → Import repo → Click Deploy → Copy URL</instructions>
   704→</task>
   705→
   706→<!-- GOOD: Claude deploys, user verifies -->
   707→<task type="auto">
   708→  <name>Deploy to Vercel</name>
   709→  <action>Run `vercel --yes`. Capture URL.</action>
   710→  <verify>vercel ls shows deployment, fetch returns 200</verify>
   711→</task>
   712→
   713→<task type="checkpoint:human-verify">
   714→  <what-built>Deployed to {url}</what-built>
   715→  <how-to-verify>Visit {url}, check homepage loads</how-to-verify>
   716→  <resume-signal>Type "approved"</resume-signal>
   717→</task>
   718→```
   719→
   720→### ❌ BAD: Too many checkpoints / ✅ GOOD: Single checkpoint
   721→
   722→```xml
   723→<!-- BAD: Checkpoint after every task -->
   724→<task type="auto">Create schema</task>
   725→<task type="checkpoint:human-verify">Check schema</task>
   726→<task type="auto">Create API route</task>
   727→<task type="checkpoint:human-verify">Check API</task>
   728→<task type="auto">Create UI form</task>
   729→<task type="checkpoint:human-verify">Check form</task>
   730→
   731→<!-- GOOD: One checkpoint at end -->
   732→<task type="auto">Create schema</task>
   733→<task type="auto">Create API route</task>
   734→<task type="auto">Create UI form</task>
   735→
   736→<task type="checkpoint:human-verify">
   737→  <what-built>Complete auth flow (schema + API + UI)</what-built>
   738→  <how-to-verify>Test full flow: register, login, access protected page</how-to-verify>
   739→  <resume-signal>Type "approved"</resume-signal>
   740→</task>
   741→```
   742→
   743→### ❌ BAD: Vague verification / ✅ GOOD: Specific steps
   744→
   745→```xml
   746→<!-- BAD -->
   747→<task type="checkpoint:human-verify">
   748→  <what-built>Dashboard</what-built>
   749→  <how-to-verify>Check it works</how-to-verify>
   750→</task>
   751→
   752→<!-- GOOD -->
   753→<task type="checkpoint:human-verify">
   754→  <what-built>Responsive dashboard - server running at http://localhost:3000</what-built>
   755→  <how-to-verify>
   756→    Visit http://localhost:3000/dashboard and verify:
   757→    1. Desktop (>1024px): Sidebar visible, content area fills remaining space
   758→    2. Tablet (768px): Sidebar collapses to icons
   759→    3. Mobile (375px): Sidebar hidden, hamburger menu in header
   760→    4. No horizontal scroll at any size
   761→  </how-to-verify>
   762→  <resume-signal>Type "approved" or describe layout issues</resume-signal>
   763→</task>
   764→```
   765→
   766→### ❌ BAD: Asking user to run CLI commands
   767→
   768→```xml
   769→<task type="checkpoint:human-action">
   770→  <action>Run database migrations</action>
   771→  <instructions>Run: npx prisma migrate deploy && npx prisma db seed</instructions>
   772→</task>
   773→```
   774→
   775→**Why bad:** Claude can run these commands. User should never execute CLI commands.
   776→
   777→### ❌ BAD: Asking user to copy values between services
   778→
   779→```xml
   780→<task type="checkpoint:human-action">
   781→  <action>Configure webhook URL in Stripe</action>
   782→  <instructions>Copy deployment URL → Stripe Dashboard → Webhooks → Add endpoint → Copy secret → Add to .env</instructions>
   783→</task>
   784→```
   785→
   786→**Why bad:** Stripe has an API. Claude should create the webhook via API and write to .env directly.
   787→
   788→</anti_patterns>
   789→
   790→<summary>
   791→
   792→Checkpoints formalize human-in-the-loop points for verification and decisions, not manual work.
   793→
   794→**The golden rule:** If Claude CAN automate it, Claude MUST automate it.
   795→
   796→**Checkpoint priority:**
   797→
   798→1. **checkpoint:human-verify** (90%) - Claude automated everything, human confirms visual/functional correctness
   799→2. **checkpoint:decision** (9%) - Human makes architectural/technology choices
   800→3. **checkpoint:human-action** (1%) - Truly unavoidable manual steps with no API/CLI
   801→
   802→**When NOT to use checkpoints:**
   803→
   804→- Things Claude can verify programmatically (tests, builds)
   805→- File operations (Claude can read files)
   806→- Code correctness (tests and static analysis)
   807→- Anything automatable via CLI/API
   808→</summary>
   809→

    43→# and fails with "Short read of FUSE request". This patch loop-reads

1→//! Folder metadata types and encryption.
     2→//!
     3→//! Matches the TypeScript `FolderMetadata` type exactly.
     4→//! Uses Serde `rename_all = "camelCase"` to produce JSON field names
     5→//! identical to the TypeScript format.
     6→//!
     7→//! Only v2 schema (per-file IPNS pointers via FilePointer) is supported.
     8→//! v1 (inline file data) has been removed.
     9→
    10→use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
    11→use thiserror::Error;
    12→use zeroize::Zeroize;
    13→
    14→use cipherbox_crypto::aes;
    15→use cipherbox_crypto::error::CryptoError;
    16→
    17→#[derive(Debug, Error)]
    18→pub enum FolderError {
    19→    #[error("Encryption failed")]
    20→    EncryptionFailed(#[from] CryptoError),
    21→    #[error("Serialization failed")]
    22→    SerializationFailed,
    23→    #[error("Deserialization failed")]
    24→    DeserializationFailed,
    25→}
    26→
    27→/// Subfolder entry within folder metadata.
    28→/// Contains ECIES-wrapped keys for accessing the subfolder.
    29→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    30→#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
    31→pub struct FolderEntry {
    32→    /// UUID for internal reference.
    33→    pub id: String,
    34→    /// Folder name (plaintext, since whole metadata is encrypted).
    35→    pub name: String,
    36→    /// IPNS name for this subfolder (k51... format).
    37→    pub ipns_name: String,
    38→    /// Hex-encoded ECIES-wrapped AES-256 key for decrypting subfolder metadata.
    39→    pub folder_key_encrypted: String,
    40→    /// Hex-encoded ECIES-wrapped Ed25519 private key for IPNS signing.
    41→    pub ipns_private_key_encrypted: String,
    42→    /// Creation timestamp (Unix ms).
    43→    pub created_at: u64,
    44→    /// Last modification timestamp (Unix ms).
    45→    pub modified_at: u64,
    46→}
    47→
    48→/// Slim file reference stored in folder metadata.
    49→/// Points to a file's own IPNS record instead of embedding all file data inline.
    50→/// Matches TypeScript `FilePointer` from `@cipherbox/crypto/file/types.ts`.
    51→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    52→#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
    53→pub struct FilePointer {
    54→    /// UUID for internal reference.
    55→    pub id: String,
    56→    /// File name (plaintext, since folder metadata is encrypted).
    57→    pub name: String,
    58→    /// IPNS name of the file's own metadata record.
    59→    pub file_meta_ipns_name: String,
    60→    /// Hex-encoded ECIES-wrapped Ed25519 private key for signing this file's IPNS record.
    61→    /// Present for files created after the random-key migration. Absent for legacy files
    62→    /// whose IPNS key is derived deterministically via HKDF.
    63→    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    64→    #[serde(default)]
    65→    pub ipns_private_key_encrypted: Option<String>,
    66→    /// Creation timestamp (Unix ms).
    67→    pub created_at: u64,
    68→    /// Last modification timestamp (Unix ms).
    69→    pub modified_at: u64,
    70→}
    71→
    72→/// A child entry can be either a folder or a file pointer.
    73→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    74→#[serde(tag = "type", rename_all = "lowercase")]
    75→pub enum FolderChild {
    76→    /// A subfolder entry.
    77→    Folder(FolderEntry),
    78→    /// A file pointer referencing a per-file IPNS record.
    79→    File(FilePointer),
    80→}
    81→
    82→/// Decrypted folder metadata structure (v2 schema with per-file IPNS pointers).
    83→/// The entire FolderMetadata object is encrypted as a single blob with AES-256-GCM.
    84→/// Children can be FolderEntry (subfolder) or FilePointer (slim IPNS reference).
    85→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    86→pub struct FolderMetadata {
    87→    /// Schema version (always "v2").
    88→    pub version: String,
    89→    /// Folders and file pointers in this folder.
    90→    pub children: Vec<FolderChild>,
    91→}
    92→
    93→/// Encrypt folder metadata with AES-256-GCM.
    94→///
    95→/// JSON serializes the metadata, then seals with AES-GCM.
    96→/// Returns the sealed bytes: IV (12) || ciphertext || tag (16).
    97→pub fn encrypt_folder_metadata(
    98→    metadata: &FolderMetadata,
    99→    folder_key: &[u8; 32],
   100→) -> Result<Vec<u8>, FolderError> {
   101→    let mut json = serde_json::to_vec(metadata).map_err(|_| FolderError::SerializationFailed)?;
   102→    let result = aes::seal_aes_gcm(&json, folder_key).map_err(FolderError::EncryptionFailed);
   103→    json.zeroize();
   104→    result
   105→}
   106→
   107→/// Decrypt folder metadata from AES-256-GCM sealed bytes.
   108→///
   109→/// Unseals, then JSON deserializes to FolderMetadata.
   110→/// Rejects metadata with version other than "v2".
   111→pub fn decrypt_folder_metadata(
   112→    sealed: &[u8],
   113→    folder_key: &[u8; 32],
   114→) -> Result<FolderMetadata, FolderError> {
   115→    let mut json = aes::unseal_aes_gcm(sealed, folder_key).map_err(FolderError::EncryptionFailed)?;
   116→
   117→    // Parse as generic JSON to check version field
   118→    let value: serde_json::Value =
   119→        serde_json::from_slice(&json).map_err(|e| {
   120→            log::error!("JSON parse failed: {}", e);
   121→            json.zeroize();
   122→            FolderError::DeserializationFailed
   123→        })?;
   124→
   125→    let version = value.get("version").and_then(|v| v.as_str());
   126→    if version != Some("v2") {
   127→        log::error!(
   128→            "Unsupported folder metadata version: {:?} (only v2 is supported)",
   129→            version
   130→        );
   131→        json.zeroize();
   132→        return Err(FolderError::DeserializationFailed);
   133→    }
   134→
   135→    let result: Result<FolderMetadata, _> = serde_json::from_value(value).map_err(|e| {
   136→        log::error!("V2 metadata deserialization failed: {}", e);
   137→        FolderError::DeserializationFailed
   138→    });
   139→
   140→    json.zeroize();
   141→    result
   142→}
   143→
   144→/// Default encryption mode for FileMetadata: "GCM".
   145→fn default_encryption_mode() -> String {
   146→    "GCM".to_string()
   147→}
   148→
   149→/// A single past version of a file.
   150→/// Stores full crypto context for independent decryption.
   151→/// Matches TypeScript `VersionEntry` from `@cipherbox/crypto/file/types.ts`.
   152→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
   153→#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
   154→pub struct VersionEntry {
   155→    /// IPFS CID of the encrypted file content for this version.
   156→    pub cid: String,
   157→    /// Hex-encoded ECIES-wrapped AES-256 key for decrypting this version.
   158→    pub file_key_encrypted: String,
   159→    /// Hex-encoded IV used for this version's encryption.
   160→    pub file_iv: String,
   161→    /// Original file size in bytes (before encryption).
   162→    pub size: u64,
   163→    /// When this version was created (Unix ms).
   164→    pub timestamp: u64,
   165→    /// Encryption mode used for this version.
   166→    pub encryption_mode: String,
   167→}
   168→
   169→/// Decrypted per-file metadata structure.
   170→/// Stored as an encrypted blob in the file's own IPNS record.
   171→/// Encrypted with the parent folder's folderKey (NOT the file's own key).
   172→/// Matches TypeScript `FileMetadata` from `@cipherbox/crypto/file/types.ts`.
   173→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
   174→#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
   175→pub struct FileMetadata {
   176→    /// Schema version.
   177→    pub version: String,
   178→    /// IPFS CID of the encrypted file content.
   179→    pub cid: String,
   180→    /// Hex-encoded ECIES-wrapped AES-256 key for decrypting file.
   181→    pub file_key_encrypted: String,
   182→    /// Hex-encoded IV used for file encryption.
   183→    pub file_iv: String,
   184→    /// Original file size in bytes (before encryption).
   185→    pub size: u64,
   186→    /// MIME type of the original file.
   187→    pub mime_type: String,
   188→    /// Encryption mode (optional for backward compat; defaults to "GCM").
   189→    #[serde(default = "default_encryption_mode")]
   190→    pub encryption_mode: String,
   191→    /// Creation timestamp (Unix ms).
   192→    pub created_at: u64,
   193→    /// Last modification timestamp (Unix ms).
   194→    pub modified_at: u64,
   195→    /// Past versions of this file (newest first). None if no versions exist.
   196→    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
   197→    #[serde(default)]
   198→    pub versions: Option<Vec<VersionEntry>>,
   199→}
   200→
   201→/// Encrypt file metadata with AES-256-GCM.
   202→///
   203→/// JSON serializes the metadata, then seals with AES-GCM.
   204→/// Uses the parent folder's folderKey for encryption.
   205→/// Returns the sealed bytes: IV (12) || ciphertext || tag (16).
   206→pub fn encrypt_file_metadata(
   207→    metadata: &FileMetadata,
   208→    folder_key: &[u8; 32],
   209→) -> Result<Vec<u8>, FolderError> {
   210→    let mut json = serde_json::to_vec(metadata).map_err(|_| FolderError::SerializationFailed)?;
   211→    let result = aes::seal_aes_gcm(&json, folder_key).map_err(FolderError::EncryptionFailed);
   212→    json.zeroize();
   213→    result
   214→}
   215→
   216→/// Decrypt file metadata from AES-256-GCM sealed bytes.
   217→///
   218→/// Uses the parent folder's folderKey for decryption.
   219→/// Unseals, then JSON deserializes to FileMetadata.
   220→pub fn decrypt_file_metadata(
   221→    sealed: &[u8],
   222→    folder_key: &[u8; 32],
   223→) -> Result<FileMetadata, FolderError> {
   224→    let mut json = aes::unseal_aes_gcm(sealed, folder_key).map_err(FolderError::EncryptionFailed)?;
   225→    let result = serde_json::from_slice(&json).map_err(|_| FolderError::DeserializationFailed);
   226→    json.zeroize();
   227→    result
   228→}

1→//! Recycle bin metadata types and encryption.
     2→//!
     3→//! Mirrors the TypeScript `RecycleBinMetadata` and `BinEntry` types from
     4→//! `@cipherbox/crypto` for cross-platform compatibility. Uses ECIES
     5→//! (same as DeviceRegistry) for encryption -- the user's secp256k1
     6→//! publicKey encrypts, privateKey decrypts.
     7→
     8→use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
     9→use thiserror::Error;
    10→
    11→use super::folder::{FilePointer, FolderEntry};
    12→
    13→#[derive(Debug, Error)]
    14→pub enum BinError {
    15→    #[error("Bin metadata encryption failed")]
    16→    EncryptionFailed,
    17→    #[error("Bin metadata decryption failed")]
    18→    DecryptionFailed,
    19→    #[error("Bin metadata serialization failed")]
    20→    SerializationFailed,
    21→    #[error("Bin metadata deserialization failed")]
    22→    DeserializationFailed,
    23→    #[error("Bin metadata validation failed: {0}")]
    24→    ValidationFailed(String),
    25→}
    26→
    27→/// Top-level recycle bin metadata structure.
    28→/// Encrypted as a whole blob via ECIES with the user's secp256k1 publicKey.
    29→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    30→#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
    31→pub struct RecycleBinMetadata {
    32→    pub version: String,
    33→    pub sequence_number: u64,
    34→    pub entries: Vec<BinEntry>,
    35→}
    36→
    37→/// A single item in the recycle bin.
    38→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    39→#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
    40→pub struct BinEntry {
    41→    pub id: String,
    42→    pub item_type: BinItemType,
    43→    pub name: String,
    44→    pub original_parent_ipns_name: String,
    45→    pub original_path: String,
    46→    pub deleted_at: u64,
    47→    pub size: u64,
    48→    pub mime_type: String,
    49→    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    50→    #[serde(default)]
    51→    pub content_cid: Option<String>,
    52→    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    53→    #[serde(default)]
    54→    pub content_size: Option<u64>,
    55→    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    56→    #[serde(default)]
    57→    pub version_cids: Option<Vec<VersionCidEntry>>,
    58→    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    59→    #[serde(default)]
    60→    pub file_pointer: Option<FilePointer>,
    61→    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    62→    #[serde(default)]
    63→    pub folder_entry: Option<FolderEntry>,
    64→}
    65→
    66→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    67→#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
    68→pub struct VersionCidEntry {
    69→    pub cid: String,
    70→    pub size: u64,
    71→}
    72→
    73→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    74→#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
    75→pub enum BinItemType {
    76→    File,
    77→    Folder,
    78→}
    79→
    80→/// Encrypt bin metadata with ECIES using user's secp256k1 public key.
    81→///
    82→/// JSON-serializes the metadata, then encrypts the entire blob with ECIES.
    83→/// Cross-compatible with TypeScript `encryptBinMetadata` from @cipherbox/crypto.
    84→pub fn encrypt_bin_metadata(
    85→    metadata: &RecycleBinMetadata,
    86→    user_public_key: &[u8],
    87→) -> Result<Vec<u8>, BinError> {
    88→    let json = serde_json::to_vec(metadata)
    89→        .map_err(|_| BinError::SerializationFailed)?;
    90→    cipherbox_crypto::ecies::wrap_key(&json, user_public_key)
    91→        .map_err(|_| BinError::EncryptionFailed)
    92→}
    93→
    94→/// Decrypt bin metadata with ECIES using user's secp256k1 private key.
    95→pub fn decrypt_bin_metadata(
    96→    ciphertext: &[u8],
    97→    user_private_key: &[u8],
    98→) -> Result<RecycleBinMetadata, BinError> {
    99→    let plaintext = cipherbox_crypto::ecies::unwrap_key(ciphertext, user_private_key)
   100→        .map_err(|_| BinError::DecryptionFailed)?;
   101→    let metadata: RecycleBinMetadata = serde_json::from_slice(&plaintext)
   102→        .map_err(|_| BinError::DeserializationFailed)?;
   103→    if metadata.version != "v1" {
   104→        return Err(BinError::ValidationFailed(
   105→            format!("Unsupported bin metadata version: {}", metadata.version),
   106→        ));
   107→    }
   108→    Ok(metadata)
   109→}
   110→
   111→/// Create a new empty RecycleBinMetadata.
   112→pub fn empty_bin_metadata() -> RecycleBinMetadata {
   113→    RecycleBinMetadata {
   114→        version: "v1".to_string(),
   115→        sequence_number: 0,
   116→        entries: vec![],
   117→    }
   118→}

1→//! IPNS record creation and marshaling.
     2→//!
     3→//! Produces IPNS records compatible with the TypeScript `ipns` npm package output.
     4→//! - CBOR-encoded data field with V2 signature
     5→//! - Protobuf-encoded IpnsEntry for marshaling
     6→//!
     7→//! IPNS name derivation has been extracted to the `cipherbox-crypto` crate
     8→//! (see `cipherbox_crypto::ipns_name::derive_ipns_name`).
     9→
    10→use std::time::{Duration, SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};
    11→
    12→use ciborium::Value as CborValue;
    13→use thiserror::Error;
    14→
    15→use cipherbox_crypto::ed25519::{get_public_key, sign_ed25519};
    16→use cipherbox_crypto::ipns_name::encode_libp2p_public_key;
    17→
    18→// Re-export derive_ipns_name for backward compatibility (tests and other code
    19→// that reference `crate::crypto::ipns::derive_ipns_name`).
    20→pub use cipherbox_crypto::ipns_name::derive_ipns_name;
    21→
    22→/// IPNS signature prefix per IPFS spec: "ipns-signature:".
    23→const IPNS_SIGNATURE_PREFIX: &[u8] = b"ipns-signature:";
    24→
    25→/// Default IPNS record TTL: 300 seconds (5 minutes) in nanoseconds.
    26→/// This matches the ipns npm package default.
    27→const DEFAULT_TTL_NS: u64 = 300_000_000_000;
    28→
    29→#[derive(Debug, Error)]
    30→pub enum IpnsError {
    31→    #[error("IPNS record creation failed")]
    32→    CreationFailed,
    33→    #[error("IPNS record marshaling failed")]
    34→    MarshalingFailed,
    35→    #[error("Invalid private key")]
    36→    InvalidPrivateKey,
    37→    #[error("Invalid public key")]
    38→    InvalidPublicKey,
    39→    #[error("CBOR encoding failed")]
    40→    CborEncodingFailed,
    41→    #[error("Signing failed")]
    42→    SigningFailed,
    43→}
    44→
    45→/// IPNS record structure matching the TypeScript IPNSRecord type.
    46→#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
    47→pub struct IpnsRecord {
    48→    /// IPFS path value (e.g., "/ipfs/bafy...").
    49→    pub value: String,
    50→    /// RFC3339 validity timestamp with nanosecond precision.
    51→    pub validity: String,
    52→    /// Validity type (0 = EOL).
    53→    pub validity_type: u32,
    54→    /// Monotonically increasing sequence number.
    55→    pub sequence: u64,
    56→    /// TTL in nanoseconds.
    57→    pub ttl: u64,
    58→    /// 64-byte Ed25519 V1 signature.
    59→    pub signature_v1: Vec<u8>,
    60→    /// 64-byte Ed25519 V2 signature.
    61→    pub signature_v2: Vec<u8>,
    62→    /// CBOR-encoded record data.
    63→    pub data: Vec<u8>,
    64→    /// 32-byte Ed25519 public key.
    65→    pub public_key: Vec<u8>,
    66→}
    67→
    68→/// Build the CBOR-encoded data field for an IPNS record.
    69→///
    70→/// The field order matches the ipns npm package: TTL, Value, Sequence, Validity, ValidityType.
    71→/// Keys are strings, values match the types used by the ipns package.
    72→fn build_cbor_data(
    73→    value: &str,
    74→    validity: &str,
    75→    sequence: u64,
    76→    ttl: u64,
    77→) -> Result<Vec<u8>, IpnsError> {
    78→    // The ipns npm package uses a CBOR map with string keys.
    79→    // Field order (matching ipns npm package output): TTL, Value, Sequence, Validity, ValidityType
    80→    //
    81→    // - TTL: unsigned integer (nanoseconds)
    82→    // - Value: byte string (the IPFS path as bytes)
    83→    // - Sequence: unsigned integer
    84→    // - Validity: byte string (RFC3339 timestamp as bytes)
    85→    // - ValidityType: unsigned integer (0 = EOL)
    86→    let cbor_map = CborValue::Map(vec![
    87→        (
    88→            CborValue::Text("TTL".to_string()),
    89→            CborValue::Integer(ttl.into()),
    90→        ),
    91→        (
    92→            CborValue::Text("Value".to_string()),
    93→            CborValue::Bytes(value.as_bytes().to_vec()),
    94→        ),
    95→        (
    96→            CborValue::Text("Sequence".to_string()),
    97→            CborValue::Integer(sequence.into()),
    98→        ),
    99→        (
   100→            CborValue::Text("Validity".to_string()),
   101→            CborValue::Bytes(validity.as_bytes().to_vec()),
   102→        ),
   103→        (
   104→            CborValue::Text("ValidityType".to_string()),
   105→            CborValue::Integer(0.into()),
   106→        ),
   107→    ]);
   108→
   109→    let mut buf = Vec::new();
   110→    ciborium::into_writer(&cbor_map, &mut buf).map_err(|_| IpnsError::CborEncodingFailed)?;
   111→    Ok(buf)
   112→}
   113→
   114→/// Format a timestamp as RFC3339 with nanosecond precision matching the ipns npm package.
   115→///
   116→/// The ipns package uses format: "2026-02-08T23:31:12.138000000Z"
   117→/// This is: full datetime + "." + 9-digit nanoseconds + "Z"
   118→fn format_validity_timestamp(validity_time: SystemTime) -> String {
   119→    let duration = validity_time
   120→        .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
   121→        .unwrap_or(Duration::ZERO);
   122→    let secs = duration.as_secs();
   123→    let nanos = duration.subsec_nanos();
   124→
   125→    // Compute date/time components from Unix timestamp
   126→    let days = secs / 86400;
   127→    let time_of_day = secs % 86400;
   128→    let hours = time_of_day / 3600;
   129→    let minutes = (time_of_day % 3600) / 60;
   130→    let seconds = time_of_day % 60;
   131→
   132→    // Convert days since epoch to date using civil_from_days algorithm
   133→    let (year, month, day) = civil_from_days(days as i64);
   134→
   135→    format!(
   136→        "{:04}-{:02}-{:02}T{:02}:{:02}:{:02}.{:09}Z",
   137→        year, month, day, hours, minutes, seconds, nanos
   138→    )
   139→}
   140→
   141→/// Convert days since Unix epoch to (year, month, day).
   142→/// Algorithm from Howard Hinnant's civil_from_days.
   143→fn civil_from_days(days: i64) -> (i64, u32, u32) {
   144→    let z = days + 719468;
   145→    let era = if z >= 0 { z } else { z - 146096 } / 146097;
   146→    let doe = (z - era * 146097) as u64; // day of era [0, 146096]
   147→    let yoe = (doe - doe / 1460 + doe / 36524 - doe / 146096) / 365; // year of era [0, 399]
   148→    let y = (yoe as i64) + era * 400;
   149→    let doy = doe - (365 * yoe + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100); // day of year [0, 365]
   150→    let mp = (5 * doy + 2) / 153; // [0, 11]
   151→    let d = doy - (153 * mp + 2) / 5 + 1; // day [1, 31]
   152→    let m = if mp < 10 { mp + 3 } else { mp - 9 }; // month [1, 12]
   153→    let y = if m <= 2 { y + 1 } else { y };
   154→    (y, m as u32, d as u32)
   155→}
   156→
   157→/// Compute the V1 signature.
   158→///
   159→/// Per IPNS spec, V1 signature is over: value_bytes + validity_bytes + varint(validityType)
   160→fn compute_v1_signature(
   161→    ed25519_private_key: &[u8; 32],
   162→    value: &str,
   163→    validity: &str,
   164→) -> Result<Vec<u8>, IpnsError> {
   165→    let mut data_to_sign = Vec::new();
   166→    data_to_sign.extend_from_slice(value.as_bytes());
   167→    data_to_sign.extend_from_slice(validity.as_bytes());
   168→    // ValidityType 0 as varint = single byte 0x00
   169→    data_to_sign.push(0x00);
   170→
   171→    sign_ed25519(&data_to_sign, ed25519_private_key).map_err(|_| IpnsError::SigningFailed)
   172→}

   174→/// Compute the V2 signature.
   175→///
   176→/// Per IPNS spec, V2 signature is over: "ipns-signature:" + cbor_data
   177→fn compute_v2_signature(
   178→    ed25519_private_key: &[u8; 32],
   179→    cbor_data: &[u8],
   180→) -> Result<Vec<u8>, IpnsError> {
   181→    let mut data_to_sign = Vec::with_capacity(IPNS_SIGNATURE_PREFIX.len() + cbor_data.len());
   182→    data_to_sign.extend_from_slice(IPNS_SIGNATURE_PREFIX);
   183→    data_to_sign.extend_from_slice(cbor_data);
   184→
   185→    sign_ed25519(&data_to_sign, ed25519_private_key).map_err(|_| IpnsError::SigningFailed)
   186→}

   188→/// Create an IPNS record signed with the given Ed25519 private key.
   189→///
   190→/// Matches the TypeScript `createIpnsRecord` with `v1Compatible: true`.
   191→pub fn create_ipns_record(
   192→    ed25519_private_key: &[u8; 32],
   193→    value: &str,
   194→    sequence_number: u64,
   195→    lifetime_ms: u64,
   196→) -> Result<IpnsRecord, IpnsError> {
   197→    // Derive public key
   198→    let public_key = get_public_key(ed25519_private_key).map_err(|_| IpnsError::InvalidPrivateKey)?;
   199→
   200→    // Compute validity timestamp
   201→    let now = SystemTime::now();
   202→    let lifetime_duration = Duration::from_millis(lifetime_ms);
   203→    let validity_time = now + lifetime_duration;
   204→    let validity = format_validity_timestamp(validity_time);
   205→
   206→    let ttl = DEFAULT_TTL_NS;
   207→
   208→    // Build CBOR data
   209→    let cbor_data = build_cbor_data(value, &validity, sequence_number, ttl)?;
   210→
   211→    // Compute V2 signature (over "ipns-signature:" + cbor_data)
   212→    let signature_v2 = compute_v2_signature(ed25519_private_key, &cbor_data)?;
   213→
   214→    // Compute V1 signature (over value + validity + varint(0))
   215→    let signature_v1 = compute_v1_signature(ed25519_private_key, value, &validity)?;
   216→
   217→    Ok(IpnsRecord {
   218→        value: value.to_string(),
   219→        validity,
   220→        validity_type: 0,
   221→        sequence: sequence_number,
   222→        ttl,
   223→        signature_v1,
   224→        signature_v2,
   225→        data: cbor_data,
   226→        public_key,
   227→    })
   228→}

   230→/// Marshal an IPNS record to protobuf bytes.
   231→///
   232→/// IpnsEntry protobuf fields:
   233→/// - field 1 (bytes): Value
   234→/// - field 2 (bytes): signatureV1
   235→/// - field 3 (enum): ValidityType (0 = EOL)
   236→/// - field 4 (bytes): Validity (RFC3339 as bytes)
   237→/// - field 5 (uint64): Sequence
   238→/// - field 6 (uint64): TTL (nanoseconds)
   239→/// - field 7 (bytes): pubKey (libp2p protobuf-wrapped Ed25519 public key)
   240→/// - field 8 (bytes): signatureV2
   241→/// - field 9 (bytes): data (CBOR)
   242→pub fn marshal_ipns_record(record: &IpnsRecord) -> Result<Vec<u8>, IpnsError> {
   243→    let mut buf = Vec::new();
   244→
   245→    // Field 1: Value (bytes, tag = 0x0a)
   246→    encode_proto_bytes(&mut buf, 1, record.value.as_bytes());
   247→
   248→    // Field 2: signatureV1 (bytes, tag = 0x12)
   249→    encode_proto_bytes(&mut buf, 2, &record.signature_v1);
   250→
   251→    // Field 3: ValidityType (enum/varint, tag = 0x18)
   252→    encode_proto_varint(&mut buf, 3, record.validity_type as u64);
   253→
   254→    // Field 4: Validity (bytes, tag = 0x22)
   255→    encode_proto_bytes(&mut buf, 4, record.validity.as_bytes());
   256→
   257→    // Field 5: Sequence (uint64, tag = 0x28)
   258→    encode_proto_varint(&mut buf, 5, record.sequence);
   259→
   260→    // Field 6: TTL (uint64, tag = 0x30)
   261→    encode_proto_varint(&mut buf, 6, record.ttl);
   262→
   263→    // Field 7: pubKey (bytes, tag = 0x3a) -- libp2p PublicKey protobuf
   264→    let libp2p_pub_key = encode_libp2p_public_key(&record.public_key);
   265→    encode_proto_bytes(&mut buf, 7, &libp2p_pub_key);
   266→
   267→    // Field 8: signatureV2 (bytes, tag = 0x42)
   268→    encode_proto_bytes(&mut buf, 8, &record.signature_v2);
   269→
   270→    // Field 9: data (bytes, tag = 0x4a) -- CBOR
   271→    encode_proto_bytes(&mut buf, 9, &record.data);
   272→
   273→    Ok(buf)
   274→}
   275→
   276→/// Encode a protobuf length-delimited (bytes) field.
   277→fn encode_proto_bytes(buf: &mut Vec<u8>, field_number: u32, data: &[u8]) {
   278→    // Tag: (field_number << 3) | 2 (wire_type = length-delimited)
   279→    encode_varint(buf, ((field_number as u64) << 3) | 2);
   280→    // Length
   281→    encode_varint(buf, data.len() as u64);
   282→    // Data
   283→    buf.extend_from_slice(data);
   284→}
   285→
   286→/// Encode a protobuf varint field.
   287→fn encode_proto_varint(buf: &mut Vec<u8>, field_number: u32, value: u64) {
   288→    // Tag: (field_number << 3) | 0 (wire_type = varint)
   289→    encode_varint(buf, ((field_number as u64) << 3) | 0);
   290→    // Value
   291→    encode_varint(buf, value);
   292→}
   293→
   294→/// Encode a varint (protobuf LEB128).
   295→fn encode_varint(buf: &mut Vec<u8>, mut value: u64) {
   296→    loop {
   297→        let byte = (value & 0x7f) as u8;
   298→        value >>= 7;
   299→        if value == 0 {
   300→            buf.push(byte);
   301→            break;
   302→        } else {
   303→            buf.push(byte | 0x80);
   304→        }
   305→    }
   306→}
